title: Encryption, Certificates and Secrets

header.html: Apply encryption at rest and in transit (2.2.1); manage certificates with ACM and Private CA (2.2.2); select client-side or server-side encryption (2.2.3); use encryption keys to encrypt and decrypt data (2.2.4); generate certificates and SSH keys for development (2.2.5); identify, mask and limit access to sensitive data (2.2.6); use secret management services (2.2.7)
the official AWS Developer Associate (DVA-C03) exam guide, Task 2.2

toc.title: Encryption at rest and in transit

html:
1Encryption at rest and in transit

State Protection
At rest Data stored on disk or in a service is encrypted (S3, EBS, DynamoDB, RDS and others support it, mostly with AWS KMS)
In transit Data moving over a network uses TLS (HTTPS)

2AWS KMS

AWS Key Management Service creates and controls encryption keys.

Concept Meaning
KMS key (formerly CMK) The key resource; the key material never leaves KMS unencrypted
AWS owned / AWS managed / customer managed keys Owned: invisible; managed: created by AWS in your account for a service; customer managed: you control the policy, rotation and deletion
Key policy The resource policy that controls who can use or manage the key (IAM alone is not enough without it)
Envelope encryption Use a data key to encrypt large data; encrypt the data key with the KMS key
Encrypt / Decrypt Direct operations on data up to 4 KB
GenerateDataKey Returns a plaintext data key and the same key encrypted; use the plaintext, then discard it and store the encrypted copy

Exam tip

. Data larger than 4 KB = envelope encryption with GenerateDataKey. Control over key rotation and policy = customer managed key.

3Server-side or client-side

Option Who encrypts When to choose
SSE-S3 S3 with S3-managed keys Simplest at-rest encryption
SSE-KMS S3 with a KMS key Need audit (CloudTrail) and key control
SSE-C S3 with a key you supply on each request You hold the keys
Client-side Your code before upload (for example, the AWS Encryption SDK) Data must be encrypted before it leaves the client

4Certificates and SSH keys

Tool Use
AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) Provision, manage and renew public TLS certificates for ELB, CloudFront, API Gateway; free for public certificates
AWS Private CA Issue private certificates for internal services and devices
EC2 key pairs / SSH keys Sign in to instances; generate for development; protect the private key

5Sensitive data and secrets

Need Tool
Store secrets (passwords, API keys) AWS Secrets Manager: automatic rotation (through Lambda), fine-grained access, encrypted with KMS, cross-Region replication; billed per secret
Store configuration and simple secrets Systems Manager Parameter Store: String, StringList, SecureString (KMS); standard tier has no charge; no built-in rotation
Find and mask personal data (PII, PHI) Amazon Macie finds sensitive data in S3; CloudWatch Logs data protection masks it; Bedrock Guardrails filters it in AI traffic; limit access with IAM, resource policies and KMS key policies [Verify live]
Exam tip

. "Rotate database credentials automatically" = Secrets Manager. "Cheap configuration values and a few secrets" = Parameter Store. Never hard-code secrets or put them in environment variables in plain text.

Exam tip

. SSE-KMS gives key control and CloudTrail audit; SSE-S3 is the simplest; SSE-C means you send the key each time.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1An application must encrypt a 5 MB file with a KMS key. What is the right approach?

  • ACall kms:Encrypt directly with the file
  • BStore the file unencrypted
  • CUse envelope encryption with GenerateDataKey
  • DUse SSH keys
Show the answer

Answer: C. Direct Encrypt is limited to 4 KB, so use a data key.

S2A team needs audit logs of every use of the encryption key for S3 objects. Which option fits?

  • ASSE-KMS
  • BSSE-S3
  • CNo encryption
  • DBase64 encoding
Show the answer

Answer: A. KMS usage is logged in CloudTrail.

S3Database credentials must rotate automatically every 30 days. Which service fits?

  • AParameter Store standard parameters
  • BEnvironment variables
  • CAWS Secrets Manager
  • DS3 Lifecycle
Show the answer

Answer: C. Secrets Manager offers built-in rotation.

S4A public website behind CloudFront needs a free managed TLS certificate that renews automatically. What fits?

  • AA self-signed certificate on each server
  • BAWS Private CA only
  • CAWS Certificate Manager
  • DSSH keys
Show the answer

Answer: C. ACM provisions and renews public certificates.

S5Data must be encrypted before it leaves the client application. Which option fits?

  • ASSE-S3
  • BA bucket policy
  • CCloudFront
  • DClient-side encryption
Show the answer

Answer: D. Client-side encryption protects data before upload.

S6A Lambda function reads an API key. What is the most secure approach?

  • ARetrieve it from Secrets Manager at runtime with a role
  • BHard-code it in the source
  • CPut it in a public repo
  • DSend it in the URL
Show the answer

Answer: A. Fetch secrets securely with a role instead of hard-coding.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is the largest payload kms:Encrypt accepts directly?

Show the answer

4 KB.

R2What does GenerateDataKey return?

Show the answer

A plaintext data key and the same key encrypted under the KMS key.

R3Which key type gives you control of rotation and policy?

Show the answer

A customer managed key.

R4Which service issues private certificates for internal use?

Show the answer

AWS Private CA.

R5Which service has built-in secret rotation?

Show the answer

Secrets Manager.

R6What does SSE-C mean?

Show the answer

S3 encrypts using a key you supply with each request.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
KMS key policy, envelope encryption, 4 KB direct limit, customer managed keys
S3 options SSE-S3, SSE-KMS (audit), SSE-C, client-side
Certificates ACM (public, renews), Private CA (internal)
Secrets Secrets Manager (rotation) vs Parameter Store (cheap, SecureString)
